Up to a square it is C_t: y² = −(6τ²+6τ+1)((2τ+1)(4τ+1)x² − (6τ+1))q(x)q(−x), q(x) = τ²x² − (6τ²+6τ+1)x + (3τ+1)², τ = t² − t, with (x, y) ↦ (x², y) onto E₂ and (x, y) ↦ (1/x², y/x³) onto E₁, so J is isogenous over ℚ to E₁ × E₂. Over ℚ(t) the pullback of P has order 12, and the gain of the gluing (the Kummer maps commute with the isogeny), computed from a half Q of 3P over the quartic field ℚ(t)(x(Q)), is a class of order 4 with coefficients in ℚ(t) whose double is not in the pullback of ⟨P⟩, so [4,12] is marked. Every 7-integral t ≡ 5 (mod 7) has J(𝔽₇) ≅ [12,12]; the kernel of E₁ → E₂ is μ₃ and 7 ≡ 1 (mod 3), so a rational point of order 3 on E₁ would give J(𝔽₇)[3] rank ≥ 3, and J(ℚ)_tors is exactly [4,12].
